related_resources.reason: Epsilon-delta limits and local inequality proofs.
Pointwise continuity, removable and jump discontinuities.
Sequential characterization of real-function continuity and limit laws.
Continuity on subsets of real numbers and the sequential formulation.

prerequisites.reason: The sequential characterization of continuity uses arbitrary convergent input sequences and the meaning of an eventual error bound. Real-number completeness is not needed to establish the local limit definitions.

recommended.reason: Reading quantified implications and their negations supports the epsilon-delta witness construction and the counterexample sequence used when continuity fails.

background: Elementary real functions, their domains, factoring differences of squares, absolute values, and inequalities. A separate completeness course is not assumed for these local continuity arguments.
readiness_checks: Can you explain why changing finitely many terms of a convergent sequence leaves its limit unchanged?
Can you factor x squared minus 1 and explain why cancelling x minus 1 is valid only away from x = 1?
Can you use |u + v| <= |u| + |v| and choose one threshold large enough for two eventual estimates?

description: Develops epsilon-delta limits and continuity through removable holes, a squared-function estimate, limit laws, and the equivalence of neighborhood and sequential definitions.
